cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Everything Has Two Prices
cards.instruction: Price every offer twice: once in practical terms and again through an emotional cost that grows when the offer returns.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll drive you for five pounds' petrol and a conversation about why you stopped calling. Please keep those two parts separate.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Here's ten. Can we leave now?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take five back. Extra petrol doesn't answer the question; tell me which evening you decided not to ring.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll call tomorrow and explain. Could I still have the lift?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Five pounds, and tell me why I should keep tomorrow free after the last three times. Please don't offer another date until you've accounted for the ones I kept.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 corrects extra money as no substitute for an answer and A5 demands accounting for kept dates, using strict expertise to escalate the emotional price of a repeated lift request.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 tomorrow promise to increase emotional exposure while keeping the practical price five pounds.

specificity.evidence: A1 petrol versus conversation separates both prices; A5 previous missed dates intelligibly explains distrust.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 asks an immediate difficult answer, not an abstract statement that emotional costs are expensive.
